rss.summary: Today, we’re announcing our research on Genie 4, our new world model that brings unprecedented realism and native audio to real-time interactive simulation.The Genie 4 m…
rss.text_excerpt: Today, we’re announcing our research on Genie 4, our new world model that brings unprecedented realism and native audio to real-time interactive simulation. The Genie 4 model incorporates and builds on capabilities from the Gemini family: Gemini Omni anchors simulations in real-world appearance and behavior, while other Gemini models provide the complex reasoning needed to help maintain a simulation’s coherence and continuity. With Genie 4, you can set an event in motion and steer scenes in real time using natural language, like moving the camera, changing the weather, or introducing new characters. Every world also generates native audio on the fly, including ambient sounds, music, and interactive dialogue. Simulating the world is a crucial step toward AGI, enabling safe training environments for robots and agents, and amplifying creative tools across industries like filmmaking, journalism, gaming, and manufacturing. We have started rolling out Genie 4 to a limited group of trusted testers. It’s coming soon to Google AI Ultra subscribers in Project Genie and early access partners in the Gemini API and AI Studio. Explore the demos on the Google DeepMind blog .

rss.text_excerpt:
When we talk about working remotely , we take a lot of things for granted, especially reliable internet and power. But sometimes, working remotely means trying to get something done on a flight, during a long train ride, or somewhere with little or no network. I moved to the foothills of the Himalayas a year ago. I love the peace of living here, but it also comes with its own challenges, including network and power outages . Things I didn’t think about as much before are now part of planning my work. I work as a Principal Engineer at Thomson Reuters , where I spend most of my time coding and reviewing my teammates’ code. Coding agents are already a big part of my everyday workflow, which made me curious about how much of that workflow I could keep using offline. Working from the foothills of the Himalayas. Photo of my workspace. If you’re someone like me, who enjoys working with technology but also finds peace in quiet, remote places where the network doesn’t always cooperate, this article is for you. It’s also for anyone who has wondered whether a coding agent can run entirely on their laptop, with the internet switched off. I tried running a coding agent locally on my laptop to see how much work I could actually get done offline. What can we do offline? A project already on your laptop gives us plenty to work with. We can ask an agent to explain an unfamiliar function, investigate a failing test, refactor a small piece of code, or help finish a feature. These tasks can run offline when the model, project dependencies and test tools are available locally. Downloading a new package or looking something up on the web will still need a connection. In our setup, its permission prompts let us review commands and changes before allowing them. In the case of GPT-6.1 Terra, OpenAI went with visual reasoning and computer use: We’re introducing GPT-6.1 Terra , a fast, efficient model that combines detailed visual reasoning and precise computer use alongside clearer, more natural writing. A significant step up from GPT‑5.6 Terra, it excels at the communication and computer-based tasks that fill the workday, from drafting proposals and interpreting technical drawings to filling out forms and editing videos. Terra sits in the same position as Sonnet in the Anthropic model collection - not the cheapest or the most expensive, making it harder to decide when to use it. Computer use is a good example of a task that benefits from a less expensive model, since you might put it to work on automated, repetitive tasks. OpenAI's Ted Sanders provided some useful advice in a comment on Hacker News: In the case of GPT-6.1 Terra, I'd say Terra is probably better than Astra and Sol at technical communication, similar on vision and computer use (but much faster!), and a bit worse on most other things. For API developers, it's a nice midrange option if you want something cheaper than Sol but a lot smarter than Luna (especially for vision / computer use / communication). For subscribers, it's not a bombshell release - if you're hitting usage limits, maybe it helps you go a bit further, and if you want clearer communication or faster computer use, it can be a nice option to select. rss.title: Greptile takes bug detection beyond code review with GPT-6 Astra
rss.summary: How Greptile uses GPT-6 Astra to test user workflows, Daybreak to strengthen security, and Codex to reduce rework.
rss.text_excerpt:
Greptile ⁠ (opens in a new window) builds AI agents that review and test code changes with full context of the codebase. “We are in the business of reducing bugs and making the world’s software more reliable,” says Co-founder and CEO Daksh Gupta. For Daksh, that mission requires testing an application’s behavior as well as reading its code, and GPT‑6 Astra’s computer use gives Greptile a way to automate testing at scale. Validating a pull request involves checking whether the code is logically correct, does what the developer intended, is secure, and avoids breaking existing functionality. For some of that testing, you need to actually run the application because reading the code alone might not reveal the problem. Daksh gives the example of a button that disappears when a website is viewed on an iPhone. With GPT‑6 Astra, Greptile can start a development server for a pull request, resize the browser to an iPhone-sized viewport, and simulate a user moving through the application. The model’s visual understanding lets it inspect the screen and spot the hidden button. “A QA firm testing all of your changes is just impractically slow considering how fast we’re able to ship code with these models,” he says. With GPT‑6 Astra, Greptile can automate this kind of application testing at scale. Daksh says more powerful models also make it easier for attackers to exploit applications, putting companies at risk, even those that previously would not have been typical targets. “We want to make it very easy for even a startup to secure their systems,” says Daksh. “With Daybreak, we’re able to do this in a way that is very safe, and we can ensure that our customers have more sophisticated defense mechanisms than the adversaries have offense mechanisms.” Greptile’s Knowledge Base indexes a company’s codebase and documents how it works in a form people and agents can read. The company makes that documentation available to Codex through a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server. This allows Codex to write code that follows the customer’s existing patterns, and thousands of customers have connected Codex to Greptile’s knowledge base, according to Daksh. rss.summary: OpenAI shares model results on the Kakeya conjecture, Exponential Time Hypothesis, and quantum chromodynamics—and how researchers can verify and build on them.

We are announcing three new discoveries in mathematics, computer science, and physics about harmonic analysis, complexity theory, and quantum field theory. Our release process continues to evolve in response to feedback from the associated academic communities. In our view, these manuscripts are best understood as a form of raw research data. To convert this raw research data into scientific understanding, in this release we are experimenting with a new approach. We reached out to external experts and asked them to act as shepherds, organizing groups to understand the new results. They advised three different release strategies: For the math result, release the AI output, leaving researchers free to organize their own efforts to explain the result. For the computer science result, form an external group of collaborators to explain the result, while making the AI output publicly available for anyone to examine and build on. For the physics result, form an external group of collaborators and defer to them on the release of materials. We do not yet know which of these three approaches will be most useful, and we welcome feedback on what works and what we can improve. The external collaborations will follow four principles: Transparency. We are transparent about the existence of our collaborations. Participants will not be asked to sign nondisclosure agreements and will be free to discuss the work, share intermediate products, and publish their conclusions. No Academic Credit. We do not seek academic credit for the discoveries produced by our internal models. Inviting a researcher to help steward a collaboration also does not imply that they or their working group made the original discovery. Recognition. This group should receive recognition for the understanding they develop, the writeups they author, and the other materials they create. The group will also help ensure that the work appropriately credits researchers, techniques, and ideas that it draws on. Independence. Participation is voluntary and unpaid. rss.title: GPT-6.1 Sol helps CodeRabbit strengthen security across complex codebases
rss.summary: CodeRabbit uses GPT-6.1 Sol to investigate security risks across complex codebases. Its security agent helps developers review findings and proposed fixes.
rss.text_excerpt: As AI accelerates software development, engineering and application-security teams need ways to investigate code changes and address vulnerabilities while keeping people in control. CodeRabbit is using GPT‑6.1 Sol as the primary model in its security agent to extend review beyond individual changes and help developers understand risks across complex codebases. A pull request can affect shared libraries, dependencies and safeguards elsewhere in an application. GPT‑6.1 Sol helps CodeRabbit connect behavior across files and components to surface potential security issues. CodeRabbit’s review is independent of the agent that wrote the code and complements established scanners. Its system also uses other frontier models and security tooling. During pull-request review, Sol helps analyze changes as developers work. In Deep Scan, it supports broader investigation across repositories, including dependencies and how components interact. CodeRabbit Secure extends that investigation to linked repositories, such as a shared authentication library, to help teams understand how a weakness could affect the wider system. # AimBuddy An on-device computer vision and control system that helps people aim in touchscreen 3D shooters. It finds people in the game picture with a neural network, outlines them, and can steer the view toward the nearest one with one extra finger. It is built for players with low vision or motor impairments, for whom fast, precise aiming on a touchscreen is the barrier. Android 11 or newer, arm64. Kotlin and Jetpack Compose for the app, C++17 for detection, tracking and control, NCNN for inference on the CPU or through Vulkan, Shizuku or root for touch access. Free and open source. ## What is technically different **The aim controller does not know the game's camera, and learns it while it aims.** How far a game's view turns per pixel of finger movement differs between games and sensitivity settings by a factor of ten or more, and the game reacts a frame or two late. A controller that assumes either figure overshoots or circles the target. `AimController` records every move it makes, `GlobalMotion` measures how the whole picture slid between frames, and `ResponseEstimator` fits the camera's gain and delay from the two by least squares. Ordinary aiming is the experiment, and nothing is calibrated by hand. Until the estimate can be trusted, only a little finger travel is allowed to be in flight, so the first move is small and its effect teaches the real figure. The controller aims at where the target will be when its move takes effect, takes its own strength down if the aim starts to swing, and lifts and re-places the finger when the game does not answer it. **The camera is read from video.** `GlobalMotion` reduces two frames to 64 by 64 grey values and finds the picture's shift by phase correlation, then polishes the strongest peaks with a few least-squares steps. Parts of the picture that do not move with the camera (the game's buttons and crosshair, the weapon, this app's own overlay) are learned and left out. So are detected people: a large one crossing the middle of the view would otherwise be mistaken for the camera turning. **A second finger on a screen that Android will not share.** The input dispatcher follows one input device at a time in a window, so a second virtual touchscreen next to the real one loses its moves whenever a real finger is down. aihot.title: OpenAI 宣布 AI 模型取得三项科学突破，涉及局部光滑猜想、指数时间假设与杨–米尔斯理论
aihot.summary: OpenAI 于 10 月 27 日宣布其 AI 模型在数学、计算机科学和物理学领域取得三项研究突破。数学上给出了所有维度下局部光滑猜想的证明，从而解决挂谷猜想与斯坦因限制猜想；计算机科学上给出推翻指数时间假设（ETH）的证明，暗示相关计算任务可能有更快算法；物理学上提出量子色动力学及标准模型一种统一完备化的严格存在性证明，涉及杨–米尔斯千禧年难题的一部分。
aihot.text_excerpt:
感谢IT之家网友 Stephen_233 、 乌蝇哥的左手 、 补药吖 的线索投递！ IT之家 10 月 27 日消息，OpenAI 宣布，其 AI 模型在数学、计算机科学和物理学领域取得三项重大突破，展现出 AI 独立发现并证明复杂科学理论的能力，而不只是回答问题或辅助研究。 在数学领域，AI 证明了适用于所有维度的局部光滑猜想，并由此解决 局部光滑猜想与挂谷猜想 。 在计算机科学领域，AI 推翻了 长期被广泛接受的指数时间假设 ，意味着未来可能找到速度更快的算法。 在物理学领域，AI 提出 量子色动力学及杨–米尔斯理论的严格数学存在性证明 ，涉及世界七大千禧年数学难题之一。 OpenAI 表示，数学和计算机科学成果已通过 Lean 数学验证工具进行形式化验证，并公开证明材料；物理学成果正由诺贝尔物理学奖得主等专家参与审查。相关成果仍需学术界进一步独立确认。 IT之家附上 OpenAI 官方的声明大意如下： 局部光滑猜想与挂谷猜想 数学方面的新成果来自调和分析领域。 1991 年，数学家克里斯托弗 · 索格提出局部光滑猜想，试图解释波在聚焦时的行为。按照该猜想，波即使出现极其强烈的聚焦，也只能持续很短的时间。如果随机选取一个具有代表性的时刻，观察到的聚焦程度总会远低于最极端的情况。 数学中经常出现类似现象：某种现象在最坏情况下可以达到非常极端的程度，但经过平均处理后，实际观察到的情况要温和得多。 局部光滑猜想描述的现象具有基础性意义，因此涉及数学分析的众多问题。其中，挂谷猜想和斯坦因限制猜想都可以由局部光滑猜想推导出来。 2019 年，古思、王虹和张睿翔证明了二维空间中的局部光滑猜想。2025 年，王虹与扎尔又证明了三维挂谷猜想。 OpenAI 的模型此次给出了局部光滑猜想在所有维度下的证明，从而也解决了所有维度下的挂谷猜想和斯坦因限制猜想。证明的关键是一种新构建的辅助偏微分方程。 OpenAI 于 2026 年 10 月 18 日获得 AI 生成的证明，并在第二天完成 Lean 形式化证明。随后，OpenAI 联系外部专家，讨论如何围绕该成果建立合作机制。 根据专家建议，OpenAI 决定直接公开 AI 生成的证明，采用与 10 月 6 日发布研究成果时相同的方式。目前，模型撰写的自然语言证明和 Lean 形式化证明均已上传至公开的 GitHub 代码仓库。 指数时间假设被推翻 计算机科学方面的发现涉及指数时间假设（ETH）。 ETH 是计算复杂性理论中一个存在已久的猜想，研究布尔公式可满足性问题的计算难度，与著名的 P 和 NP 问题密切相关。 长期以来，学术界 普遍认为 ETH 成立 。数百篇研究论文以该假设为前提，推导出图论、计算生物学、数据库和计算几何等领域的计算难度结论。 近期，OpenAI 的系统却 给出了 ETH 不成立的证明 ，并通过 Lean 完成了形式化验证。 ETH 被推翻后，研究人员需要重新审视许多计算任务 究竟还能获得多大幅度的速度提升 。新成果也有助于指导更高效算法的研究。不过，要找到能够实现这些提升的算法，并将理论成果转化为实际应用，仍需要大量后续研究。 OpenAI 邀请三位算法设计和计算复杂性理论专家牵头，负责验证、研究和解释这项成果，分别是加利福尼亚大学圣迭戈分校的拉塞尔 · 因帕利亚佐和拉马莫汉 · 帕图里，以及麻省理工学院的瑞安 · 威廉姆斯。 三位专家在该领域都有长期研究积累： OpenAI 接受了合作团队提出的两项要求：首先，公开研究成果的所有原始数据，方便其他研究人员独立验证；其次，由 OpenAI 提供资金，举办一场学术会议，讨论新成果对计算机科学领域的整体影响。 合作团队还邀请学术界共同组织对 ETH 证明的公开审查，并就 AI 研究突破引发的问题展开讨论，包括如何验证成果、如何开放研究资料、如何认定学术贡献，以及未来应如何开展科研工作。 OpenAI 于 10 月 16 日生成了推翻 ETH 的自然语言证明，10 月 17 日又完成了 Lean 形式化证明。随后，OpenAI 开始着手建立前述外部合作机制。 模型生成的自然语言证明 和 Lean 证明 现已在 OpenAI 的公开 GitHub 代码仓库发布。 量子色动力学的存在性与标准模型的统一完备化 物理学方面，OpenAI 提出了一项关于量子场论存在性的研究成果。 该成果从严格的数学意义上，证明了四维空间中某些 包含规范场和费米子的相互作用量子场论确实存在 ，其中包括量子色动力学（QCD），以及粒子物理学标准模型的一种统一完备化理论。 证明采用了构造性量子场论中巴拉班提出的研究方法。此外，研究还解决了一个子问题，即证明纯杨-米尔斯理论的存在性。该问题属于克雷数学研究所设立的量子杨-米尔斯理论千禧年大奖难题的一部分。 粒子物理学标准模型描述了亚原子基本粒子之间的相互作用，涵盖自然界四种基本相互作用中的三种，不包括引力。 由于标准模型本身无法直接推广至任意短的距离尺度，OpenAI 的存在性证明针对的是 包含标准模型规范场和费米子的最简单大统一理论 。 量子色动力学研究夸克、胶子等粒子如何通过强相互作用发生联系。纯杨-米尔斯理论研究的范围更窄，只涉及传递强相互作用的胶子之间的自相互作用，不包括夸克等物质粒子。 OpenAI 邀请大卫 · 格罗斯牵头研究，团队其他成员包括迈克尔 · 道格拉斯、阿瑟 · 贾菲、伊戈尔 · 克莱巴诺夫和尼基塔 · 涅克拉索夫。 五位学者在量子场论及数学物理领域均有重要贡献： 大卫 · 格罗斯： 1973 年，他参与的杨-米尔斯理论渐近自由研究，为量子色动力学成为公认的强相互作用理论奠定了基础，并使他获得 2004 aihot.text_excerpt:
Anthropic has finally filed its S-1 prospectus with the SEC, a document designed to give investors a look under the hood of its business, from how much its executives are making and plans for spending its IPO billions to the risks that could derail its ambitions. At more than 300 pages, there’s a lot to unpack, and some of the disclosures have not previously been reported. Here are some of the biggest things that jumped out to us from our first pass: Sibling co-founders Dario Amodei and Daniela Amodei are the two most highly-paid executives at Anthropic, according to the filing. Last year, CEO Dario’s compensation totaled nearly $18 million, most of which came from stock and option awards. President Daniela, meanwhile, received $16.4 million. Admittedly, it is at the lower end of the Big Tech scale , but it is still a tidy sum. And that’s not all. Anthropic also spent $2.75 million on “personal security services” for Dario and $1.29 million for “personal protection, home security, and transportation services” for Daniela. Dario also gets access to a private jet for personal use, which cost the company another $97,055. The company says its success is “highly dependent on the continued service” of its senior team, particularly Dario and Daniela, who “are critical” to advancing the company’s research and mission. Anthropic has some pretty existential risk factors Every S-1 features a long list of things that could go wrong. Anthropic’s is no exception. But alongside standard warnings about competition, regulation, and market shifts, there are some less conventional risks too. For one, Anthropic warns that AI systems could cause potentially “catastrophic” harm, potentially of a kind that could not be underwritten by the entire “insurance industry in the aggregate.” As AI systems become more sophisticated, there’s also the question of whether Claude — or any other AI system — could possess or develop “forms of sentience.” Such a scenario would present some rather unusual business challenges. There’s also the possibility they “may behave in unintended, misaligned, or autonomous ways” that could damage the company. It’s no secret that Anthropic needs compute, but the sheer scale of its spending is staggering.
